title: Bacteriophage Infectivity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa Biofilm under Different pH Conditions
content: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is one of the most common pathogens of nosocomial infection; they are capable of acquiring multidrug resistance and forming robust biofilms. Various environmental factors can affect the formation and growth of biofilm, one crucial parameter is the pH value [1]. The body fluid environment must have an appropriate pH to maintain a normal metabolism and physiological functions. However, different parts of the human body show large differences in pH, for example, the pH value of the bone is weakly alkaline, while the pH value of saliva from the mouth is acidic [2]. P. aeruginosa can infect and form biofilms on various human organs that have different pH values, such as skin, lung, and the urinary tract [3]. Here, we choose the laboratory reference strain P. aeruginosa (PAO1) as a paradigm strain for investigating bacteriophage infectivity against biofilms at different pH. As antimicrobal agents we used virulent bacteriophages of the PB1 species (Caudoviricetes; Pbunavirus; Pbunavirus PB1). PB1-like bacteriophages are a usual component of phage cocktails, which have a wide range of lytic activity and a relatively low frequency of phage resistant mutant generation [4]. In our study, we evaluate the effects of biofilm-phage interactions at different pH.
